explanation: The thrown error inside `try` aborts that block immediately, so `console.log('unreachable')` never runs. Control jumps straight to `catch`, which logs the caught message. `finally` always runs after `try`/`catch` settles, whether or not an error was thrown or caught, so 'cleanup' logs next. Since `catch` handled the error (no rethrow), the function returns normally and execution continues past the try/catch/finally block to 'after'.
prompt: Drag these console.log outputs into the order they actually print when process() runs.
